title: Embryological facts follow from late-appearing variations inherited at corresponding ages

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Embryological facts follow from late-appearing variations inherited at corresponding ages

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The leading facts of embryology are explained because, in the descendants of a common progenitor, successive slight modifications generally do not appear at a very early period of life (though they may be caused earlier) and are inherited at a corresponding later age, leaving embryos little modified.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. XIII: Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: the leading facts in embryology, which are second in importance to none in natural history, are explained on the principle of slight modifications not appearing, in the many descendants from some one ancient progenitor, at a very early period in the life of each, though perhaps caused at the earliest, and being inherited at a corresponding not early period.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XIII, “Mutual Affinities of Organic Beings: Morphology: Embryology: Rudimentary Organs”; section “EMBRYOLOGY, laws of, explained by variations not supervening at an early age, and being inherited at a corresponding age”. Scope: animals generally

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch13-21: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.59

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern developmental time series provide a direct test for selected species. Current coverage is too narrow to explain the leading facts of embryology across animals generally.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Across related species, estimate developmental onset of derived phenotypic and gene-expression differences and test whether onset timing is conserved between parents and offspring and biased toward later stages. The joint late-onset and corresponding-age pattern supports the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cause, first phenotypic appearance and inheritance timing are distinct variables.

Comparable developmental staging across species is difficult.

Public time series cover few clades.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.68
data adequacy: 0.45
analysis feasibility: 0.48
discriminating power: 0.62
operationalizability: 0.68

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The timing of first appearance of species differences is measurable in public expression series for a few well-studied animals. That timing does not separate late origin of variation from early origin plus later inheritance or from selective removal of early changes. The mechanism as a general explanation of embryology is therefore only partly constrained by existing data, and extending it past model species would be a long compilation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure when, in ontogeny, differences among related species first appear in morphology and gene expression, and whether the genetic variants that distinguish them are expressed at that same later age. The claim is confirmed if species differences and their underlying variants are systematically late and embryos remain comparatively uniform, and refuted if most differences are already present at the earliest stages.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Showing that a variant is inherited at a corresponding age requires pedigrees or experimental crosses that are available for very few traits.

Early embryonic similarity can be produced by selection removing early variants, which yields the same pattern without variations originating late.

Expression-timing and mapping data exist for a handful of model animals, not for animals generally.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.4
data existence: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.5
data adequacy: 0.4
analysis feasibility: 0.4
